notes: Completed 30-day Hosted API trial covering chat UX, doc search and rerank. Trial started 2024-10-01.
Observed averages: baseline traffic 18 QPS during working hours; weekend baseline ~6 QPS.
Burst profile: recurring short bursts up to 250 QPS for 60-180 seconds triggered by push notifications and in-app campaigns.
Token profile measured: ~55% short requests (<=64 tokens), ~30% medium (65-512 tokens), ~15% long (>512 tokens). Avg tokens/request ~420 (includes prompt + context).
Latency notes: short-chat p50 ~120ms, p95 ~380ms on hosted; long summaries p95 up to ~1.1s. Customer target: p95 <= 400ms for short chat use case.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget but open to 12-month commit if burst pricing and autoscale caps are favorable.
POC findings: prefix/KV cache test reduced prompt tokens by ~25% for FAQ flows; rerank workload benefited from quantized model with ~28% cost savings but slight throughput hit.
Security: strong requirement for VPC peering + KMS; want SOC2 attestation plus a short window for audit log export to SIEM.
Infra ask: detailed capacity plan showing node counts for sustained load vs burst, spin-up latency for burst pool, and fallback plan to hosted API if Dedicated saturated.
Legal: retention and deletion SLA questions raised; need template language for 30/90/365 day retention options.
Finance: requested 3 pricing scenarios (12m commit, 6m commit, pay-as-you-go with burst cap) for comparison vs incumbent vendor.

SE recommendation from 2024-11-12 call: initial Dedicated pool = 6 x A40/A100-equivalent for sustained 30 QPS with p95 headroom; burst pool = 12-20 nodes for peak 250 QPS. Consider autoscale warm pool to reduce cold-start latency.
Internal risk: longer-context summarization shows occasional quality drift vs baseline model; recommended Redwood Optimize eval set to gate any quantized model rollout.
Sales approach: phased deployment (dev -> staging -> canary -> prod) with documented rollback and automatic fallback routes.
